texts.preamble: Da vs . Amar Chand Page 1 Of 10 on 31 August, 2015 In The Court Of Gaurav Rao Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrateii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi C.C. No. 200/11 Complaint U/S 16 Of The Prevention Of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 Food Inspector Department of Pfa Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20, Lawrence Road Indl. Area, Delhi - 35 ........ Complainant Versus Amar Chand s/o Bhag Chand M/s Jain Stores, Shop no. 259/19, Tughlakabad Extension, New Delhi110019 R/o 2856/32, Tughlakabad Extension, New Delhi110019 ........ Vendorcum Proprietor Serial number of the case : 200/11 Date of the commission of the offence : 18.06.2011 Date of filing of the complaint : 14.11.2011 Name of the Complainant : Sh. P.M. Kothekar, Food Inspector Cc No. 200/11 Da Vs. Amar Chand Page 1 of 10 Offence complained of or proved : Section 2 (ia) (a) (b) (f) & (m) of Pfa Act 1954, punishable U/s 16(1A) r/w section 7 of the Pfa Act. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Final order : Accused acquitted. Da vs . Amar Chand Page 1 Of 10 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198408758/ 1
texts.facts: In brief the case of the prosecution is that on 18.06.2011 at about 07.30 p.m. Food Inspector P.M. Kothekar and Field Assistant Sh. S. Messy under the supervision and directions of SDM / LHA Sh. Kuldeep Singh visited M/s Jain Store, Shop no. 259/19, Tughlakabad Extension, New Delhi where accused Amar Chand who was the Vendorcum proprietor was found present conducting the business of sale of various food articles including Chana Dal ready for sale for human consumption and in compliance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, the Food Inspector collected / purchased the sample of Chana Dal. 2. It is further the prosecution's case that the sample was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst the sample was adulterated because it was containing five living insects and accordingly after obtaining the necessary Sanction / Consent under Section 20 of the Act the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of Section 2 (ia) (a) (b) (f) & (m) of PFA Act 1954 punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w Section 7 of the Act. 3. After the complaint was filed, the accused was summoned vide orders dated 14.11.2011. 4. Prosecution led the precharge evidence wherein FI Sh. P.M. Kothekar was examined as PW1 and precharge evidence was closed vide orders dated 11.03.2014. 5. Charge for violation of provision of Section 2 (ia) (a) (b) (f) & (m) of PFA Act 1954 punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w section 7 of the Act was framed against the accused persons vide order dated 08.07.2015 to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. The complainant/prosecution so far examined one witness i.e. Sh. P.M. Kothekar as PW1. A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under: 8. PW1 Food Inspector P.M. Kothekar deposed that on 18.06.2011 he was posted as FI in Sub Division Kalkaji Delhi and on that day he alongwith FA Shri S. Massey under the supervision of SDM / LHA Shri Kuldeep Singh visited the premises of M/s Jain Store, Shop No. 259/19, Tughlakabad Extension, New Delhi, where accused Amar Chand was found conducting the business of above mentioned shop, having stored various grocery items including Chana Dal for sale for human consumption. He deposed that this Chana Dal was lying in an open gunny bag bearing no label or declaration. He deposed that first of all he disclosed his identity to the accused / vendor Amar Chand and after inspection of the shop, he expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Chana Dal from him for analysis to which he agreed. Da vs . Amar Chand Page 1 Of 10 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198408758/ 2 He deposed that before starting the sample proceedings he tried to associate some public witnesses in sample proceedings by requesting some customers and neighbouring shopkeepers, but none came forward. He deposed that then, on his request FA Shri S. Massey agreed and joined as witness in sample proceedings. He deposed that thereafter, at about 07.30 PM he purchased from the accused / vendor 3 Kg of Chana Dal, which was taken from above mentioned gunny bag, on payment of Rs. 102/ vide Vendor's Receipt Ex. PW 1/A, bearing signature of vendor at point A. He deposed that the sample was taken after properly mixing the Dal Chana with the help of a clean and dry jhaba by rotating it in all possible directions in the gunny bag itself several times and then 3 Kg of Chana Dal was taken out from the entire mixed lot and was divided equal parts and was put into three clean and dry sample glass bottles. He deposed that all the three sample bottles were separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed as per PFA Act & Rules and LHA slips bearing signature and Code No. of LHA Shri Kuldeep Singh were affixed on all the three counterparts from top to bottom. He deposed that the vendor signed on each counterpart in such a manner so as to appear partly on LHA slips and partly on wrapper of the counterparts. He deposed that Notice in Form VI Ex. PW1/B was prepared and vendor made endorsement on this notice at Portion X to X that sample commodity was ready for sale and he had no bill of the purchase of the same. He deposed that a copy of this Notice was given to the vendor as per his acknowledgment thereon at portion Y to Y. He deposed that Panchnama Ex. PW1/C was prepared. He deposed that all these documents were read over and explained to the vendor in Hindi in vernacular and after understanding the same, he signed the same at point A, witness signed the same at point B and he signed the same at point C. He deposed that raid report under Rule 9(e) Ex. PW1/D was prepared bearing signature of LHA at point A, signature of witness at point B and my signature at point C. He deposed that on the next working day i.e. 20.06.2011 one counterpart alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VII in a separate sealed cover were deposited with PA vide PA's Receipt Ex. PW 1/E and the remaining two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA on 20.06.2011 vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW 1/F, bearing his signature at point A and signature of LHA at point B, under intimation that one counterpart of the sample has already been deposited with the PA. He deposed that all the copies of Memo in Form VII were marked with Seal Impression with which the sample counterparts were sealed. He deposed that PA Report Ex. PW1/G was received which revealed that the sample was adulterated and accordingly on the directions of SDM / LHA he started the investigations. He deposed that during investigation he sent a letter to vendor vide Ex. PW 1/H through registered post and received its reply vide Ex. PW1/H1 to the effect that vendor was the sole proprietor of M/s Jain Store and his shop was not registered with Sales Tax or MCD. Along with this reply he received photocopy of Voter I card of vendor which is Ex. P1. He deposed that he sent a letter Ex. PW1/I VATO, Ward No. 90 for seeking information on the constitution of M/s Jain Store, Shop No. 259/19, Tughlakabad Extension, New Delhi and received its reply at portion X to X on the same that said firm was registered in that Ward. He deposed that on conclusions of investigations he found that accused Amar Chand was the sole proprietor of above mentioned firm and was responsible for conducting its day to day business. He deposed that thereafter he put the entire case file before the concerned SDM / LHA, who forwarded the same to the then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent and the then Director PFA Shri K.S. Singh granted his Consent for prosecution of accused after applying his mind vide Ex. PW 1/J, bearing his signature at point A. He deposed that then he filed the complaint before this Court vide Ex. PW 1/K, bearing his signature at Da vs . Amar Chand Page 1 Of 10 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198408758/ 3 point A. He deposed that then Intimation letter Ex. PW1/L alongwith copy of PA's report was sent to the accused through registered post through DO which was not received back undelivered. Photocopies of Postal Registration Receipts are collectively Ex. PW 1/M, bearing relevant entry at point A. During his cross examination he stated that no live or dead insects were visible to him with naked eyes when he lifted the sample of Chana Dal from the accused.
texts.arguments: 15. In New Delhi Municipal Committee Vs. Chaman Lal and the State FAC 1980 (1) 272, the Hon. Delhi High Court held as under: "........As to the connotation of the expression "insectinfested" the Supreme Court put its seal of approval on the Bench decision of this court in Dhanraj vs. Municipal Corporation of Delhi, 1972 FAC 335 in which Jagjit Singh, J had brought out the whole position quite lucidly. To be concise it was held by the Division Bench that "an article of food would be insectinfested" if it has been attacked by insects in swarms or numbers, if an article of food is attacked by insects in large swarms or numbers and for some reason those insects die, the mere fact that the article of food has no longer living insects but has dead insects will not change its character of being insectinfested". The number of insects present was by no means large". 16. In Dhan Raj's case (Supra), the Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held as under: "The expression "insectinfested" was not defined in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and has, therefore, to be given its ordinary meanings. The word "infest" appears to have been derived from the latin word "infestare" which meant to assail or molest. According to the Oxford English Dictionary (Volume V at page 259 the word "infest" means to "To attack, assail, annoy, or trouble (a person or thing) in a persistent manner;" to visit persistently or in large numbers for purposes of destruction or plunder;" "to swarm in or about, so as to be troublesome". 'In the same Dictionary the word "infestation" is stated to mean; "The action of infesting, Da vs . Amar Chand Page 1 Of 10 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198408758/ 4 assailing, harassing, or persistently molesting". It is also mentioned that the word is now used especially for "insects which attack plants, grain etc. in large swarms". Thus an article of food would be "insectinfested", if it has been attacked by insects in swarms or numbers." 17. In State (Delhi Admn.) v. Puran Mal, 1985(2) C.L.R. 483 the Hon. Apex Court discussed the meaning of "infest" as under: "....According to Webster's New World Dictionary 'infest' means "to overrun or inhabit in large numbers, usually so as to be harmful or bothersome, swarm in or about"..... 8. According to Webster's Illustrated Contemporary Dictionary (Encyclopedic Edition), 'infest' means "to overrun or spread in large numbers so as to be unpleasant or unsafe" 18.
